name: Wang Zhenjian
current_role: Chairman, Chongqing Shunbo Aluminum Co., Ltd. (顺博合金, SZSE: 002996)
profile: Wang Zhenjian (王真见, b. 1964) is chairman and co-controlling shareholder (~20.5%) of Shunbo Aluminum, one of China's top-four recycled aluminium alloy producers, with plants in Chongqing, Qingyuan, Liyang, Xiangyang and Anhui. He has 30+ years in scrap-metal recycling; the company listed in Shenzhen in Aug 2020.
interesting_fact: Shunbo is a pure recycled-aluminium (circular-economy) business: it turns scrap aluminium into alloy ingots for auto and motorcycle parts, and produced ~553,000 tonnes of alloy ingot in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shunbo he worked at the Xilu metal fittings factory in Yongkang, Zhejiang, then ran the Xilu metal processing plant in Chongqing's Jiulongpo district as factory director; he was vice-chairman of Shunbo Ltd from 2008 and chairman since May 2013.
notes: Low public profile; no personal media presence found. Controls company jointly with Wang Zengchao and Wang Qi. Best route is the board secretary via ir@sballoy.com (Chinese-language).

name: Ren Rui
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (~2.4%, end-2024) of Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology (CVTE, SZSE: 002841); formerly chairman of its supervisory board
profile: Ren Rui (任锐, b. 1977) is one of CVTE's five original founders and an engineer by background. He was chief engineer of the TV products division and chaired CVTE's supervisory board from 2011; CVTE (Seewo, MAXHUB brands) listed in Shenzhen in 2017. He no longer appears among current officers but remains a top-10 shareholder.
interesting_fact: CVTE began in Dec 2005 when five people, Ren Rui among them, each put in RMB 200,000 to form a company with RMB 1m registered capital; it is now a leading maker of LCD TV controller boards and interactive flat panels.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding CVTE he worked as an engineer at Amoi (Xiaxin Electronics), Guangzhou Lehua Electronics and Guangzhou Chixun, then joined CVTE at its founding as deputy chief engineer of the TV products division.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal media/social accounts found. Only route is via CVTE board office (shiyuan@cvte.com). Not to be confused with other people named Ren Rui.

name: Victor Perlroth
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Kodiak Sciences Inc. (Nasdaq: KOD), Palo Alto
profile: Victor Perlroth, M.D. (Princeton A.B. molecular biology; Stanford M.D./M.B.A.) co-founded Kodiak Sciences in 2009 and leads it as chairman and CEO, developing long-acting retinal drugs for wet AMD and diabetic eye disease. He earlier co-founded Avidia, sold to Amgen for $450m, then worked in life-sciences venture capital.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Kodiak said its tarcocimab (Zenkuda) and tabirafusp-ted met primary endpoints in the pivotal DAYBREAK wet-AMD trial, with most Zenkuda patients on a 24-week dosing interval.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was chief operating officer of Guzik Technical Enterprises, a maker of test equipment for the hard-disk-drive industry; he graduated summa cum laude from Princeton in molecular biology.
notes: Wealth is mostly KOD stock (volatile biotech). Kodiak IR site (ir.kodiak.com) blocks automated fetches, so IR/media contacts could not be read; company general email info@kodiak.com is published in the site footer.

name: Shao Yixing
current_role: Private investor; shareholder (~3.8% in 2022) of Aerospace CH UAV Co. (航天彩虹, SZSE: 002389, formerly Zhejiang Nanyang Technology); no company role since Dec 2022
profile: Shao Yixing (邵奕兴, b. 1987) is the son of Shao Yutian, founder of Zhejiang Nanyang Technology, a Wenling (Taizhou) maker of capacitor and optical films. Father and son jointly controlled ~42%; in 2016 the father sold 21% to a Taizhou state investor, and China Aerospace (CASC) later took control. Shao was executive VP until resigning in Dec 2022.
interesting_fact: The family's plastic-film company became the listed vehicle for China Aerospace's Rainbow (CH) drone business; renamed Aerospace CH UAV, it now makes the CH-3/CH-4 drones alongside film materials.
notes: No current executive role or public profile; on resignation (Dec 2022) the company thanked him for his contributions to Nanyang and CH UAV (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk03/finalpage/2023-03-29/55dac1e6-3745-4a69-b856-1f889d8aef7b.PDF is 2022 AR; resignation notice: https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk03/finalpage/2023-01-02/d6ea13b9-8f28-41ea-a3cd-68b43d174368.PDF). No published contact route found.

name: Michael Douglas
current_role: Actor and film producer (announced retirement from acting in 2025); UN Messenger of Peace; board member, Nuclear Threat Initiative
profile: Michael Douglas (b. 1944), son of Kirk Douglas, won Best Picture as producer of One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest and Best Actor as Gordon Gekko in Wall Street. Listed with wife Catherine Zeta-Jones on the UK rich list; his wealth comes from acting and producing. He is a long-time nuclear-disarmament advocate.
interesting_fact: He produced and starred in The China Syndrome (1979), a thriller about a nuclear power plant accident; the Three Mile Island accident happened just 12 days after the film's release.
deep_cut_fact: He worked three summers during college at the Eugene O'Neill Theater Center in Waterford, Connecticut, and remains a longstanding board member there; he also hosted a celebrity golf tournament for 12 years that raised $10m+ for the Motion Picture & Television Fund.
notes: Major celebrity; outreach realistically goes through his talent agency/publicist (not verified here due to search limits). Angle for an energy podcast: China Syndrome and his Nuclear Threat Initiative board work. Profile here is about him alone, not Zeta-Jones.

name: David Crossland
current_role: Jersey-based private investor; founder and former chairman of Airtours/MyTravel Group
profile: David Crossland (b. 1946), from east Lancashire, founded Airtours in 1972 by buying two small travel shops in Nelson, then built it into MyTravel, a global package-holiday group with its own charter airline, which merged with Thomas Cook AG in 2007. He now lives in Jersey and invests privately (travel and investment per the rich list).
interesting_fact: Airtours' first two shops (Pendle Travel Services, Nelson) were bought from an elderly couple, with half the money borrowed from his brother-in-law; Airtours later launched its own airline in 1990 and offered £299 Caribbean charters.
deep_cut_fact: He left Burnley Grammar School with three O-levels and his first job, in August 1963, was at the travel agency inside the Colne Co-operative Society's Colne Hall offices on Albert Road, where he learnt the trade.
notes: Private; no published personal/office contact found (web search budget ran out mid-lane, so current business interests were not re-verified). Alive status assumed from no death record on Wikipedia.

name: Anastasios Gianakakos
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chair, Kardigan, Inc. (Nasdaq: KARD), South San Francisco
profile: Anastasios 'Tassos' Gianakakos (MIT engineering & economics; Northwestern biotech; Harvard MBA) was CEO of MyoKardia, sold to Bristol Myers Squibb for $13.1bn in 2020. He then co-founded Prolaio (connected cardiac care) and Kardigan, a cardiovascular drug developer with three late-stage programs that listed on Nasdaq.
interesting_fact: Kardigan folds Prolaio's AI and real-world-data platform into drug development, aiming to cut the time and cost of cardiovascular trials; MyoKardia's $13.1bn exit was one of the largest cardiology biotech deals.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in vaccine development at Merck & Co. before helping start and scale several biotech companies.
notes: Goes by 'Tassos'. Contact form has a 'Media' inquiry option. Company website is kardigan.bio (kardigan.com is an unrelated parked domain).

name: Jeremy Peace
current_role: Private investor; former chairman and owner of West Bromwich Albion FC (sold 2016)
profile: Jeremy Peace (b. 1956, West Bromwich) is a former stockbroker and investment banker turned small-cap dealmaker (Morland Securities, Quadrant Group, London Town, Galahad Capital). He joined West Bromwich Albion's board in 2000, became chairman in 2002, took the club private in 2005 and sold it to Guochuan Lai in 2016 for an estimated £150m-£200m.
interesting_fact: A West Bromwich native, he bought into and ran his hometown club for 16 years before selling it to Chinese businessman Guochuan Lai in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before football he was a major shareholder and director of Morland Securities, later renamed Access Satellite International, and of Sangers Photographics (later Quadrant Group), after working in accountancy, stockbroking and investment banking from 1974 to 1983.
notes: Famously media-shy; no published contact found. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so current activities were not re-verified beyond Wikipedia.
